quizzes.question: What was the central flaw of the Newcomen engine that Watt identified?
options: It could not be built large enough
The same chamber was heated and cooled every cycle
It required too many skilled operators
Its cylinder was made of the wrong metal
quizzes.explanation: Newcomen's engines had been pumping mine water for decades before Watt was handed a model to repair — nobody had thought the waste worth fixing because coal at the pithead was almost free.

quizzes.question: How much fuel did Watt's improved design use compared with a Newcomen engine doing the same work?
quizzes.explanation: The saving was what sold the engines: Boulton and Watt often charged customers a share of the fuel they no longer burned.

quizzes.question: Which group near Birmingham did Watt join to discuss science and its practical uses?
quizzes.explanation: The Lunar Society was informal and met in members' houses, yet its conversations shaped much of British industry — Boulton was part of the same circle.

polls.question: Watt had the invention, Boulton the capital and the workshops. Whose contribution mattered more to the engine's success?
Watt was skeptical that his engine belonged in transport. Why do you think he held back?
options: He doubted it could be made safe
He was absorbed in factory work

polls.question: The industrial revolution brought wealth along with overcrowding, pollution and child labour. How would you weigh it?
options: Too early to judge even now

choices.prompt: You have a working model that quarters the fuel bill, but no capital and no factory. Boulton offers a partnership on his terms. What would you do?
Around 1800 Watt handed the business to his son and others. In his place, what would you have done?
